title: latex options?
description:
Do you know how to include unicode emoji in LaTeX (pdf) output?

If you happen to know how, I think it would be a good idea to include instructions for how to include unicode emoji in LaTeX documents (such as from `.Rmd` files, using `knitr` with `tinytex` or MiKTeX or LiveTeX, many combinations).

Example:

````
---
title: "Some_title"
output:
  rmarkdown::pdf_document:
    latex_engine: xelatex
header-includes:
  - \usepackage{graphicx} 
---

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(kableExtra)
data.frame(
  Name = c("John", "Jane", "Alice"),
  Q1 = c("grinning", "pensive", ""),
  Q2 = c("pensive", "", "grinning")
) |>
  mutate(across(-Name, ~ coalesce(emoji::emoji_name[.x], ""))) |>
  kable(format="latex") |>
  kable_styling()
```
````

This renders without error (due to the `xelatex` engine) but does not show the emoji themselves.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/acc333e9-ce36-4e62-b644-646821f89b07)

(Inspired by https://stackoverflow.com/q/79572460/3358272.)

title: Replace emojis with text description
description:
``` r
library(emoji)

example <- c(
  "These are emojis; 🤦 and 🤦🏼",
  "You can write slides in 🔑🎵"
)

emoji_dict <- setNames(
  paste0(":", names(emoji::emoji_name), ":"),
  unname(emoji::emoji_name)
)

emoji_dict <- emoji_dict[-c(3865, 3866)] #these two emojis mess things up
emoji_dict <- rev(sort(emoji_dict)) #make sure emojis with qualifiers gets replaces first

stringr::str_replace_all(
  example, 
  emoji_dict
)
#> [1] "These are emojis; :person_facepalming: and :person_facepalming::medium_light_skin_tone:"
#> [2] "You can write slides in :key::musical_note:"
```

<sup>Created on 2023-02-09 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>
